Buildings block shots, Xbox controller support, gyro aim. Asymmetric mechs are in a dev build: Iron Stride Squad v0.5-dev.

games.name: Red Deer Rich · phone mode
games.notes: Play on one phone: the phone hosts the game, board on top with pinch / drag and a soft camera that glides to the action and eases out the moment you touch it, tabs along the bottom open a small sheet (swipe up for everything, down or tap outside to close), tiny dice icon + shake to roll, small QR in the corner so friends join from their own phones. Move to TV: scan a TV's 0-Phi QR (front door) or type the TV's room code, the phones vote (majority), the whole game moves to the TV and every phone becomes a normal TV controller with the same seat. Live v0.8 untouched. Before release: real-phone test over the internet, then show Red Deer Rich as Plays on your phone on the front door.

games.name: Orbit Brawl
games.notes: v0.1: phone-first first-person space dogfighter. Each phone is a cockpit with twin floating sticks: left flies (forward/back + strafe), right turns (pitch + yaw). Gear: swap sticks, invert up/down and left/right, right stick rolls instead of yaw; an Xbox controller also works (RT gun, LT hold-to-charge bomb). GUN button on the left, hold BOMB on the right (charge = farther throw, bigger blast). Shields flash and rattle the phone, then hull damage, then destroyed and respawn in 3 s. Free-for-all 3-minute rounds, 2-20 pilots, bots fill to 8. Asteroid field, nebula sky, soft arena edge. Phone only (vs bots, or host friends from your phone): the round ends with up to 3 action replays (your kills and streaks, big bombs). On a TV the screen is a live cinematic camera (chase, fly-by, duel and wide shots, cutting to bombs and kills) with scores and kill feed; phones stay the cockpits. Proxy pods; drop Justin's pod in as orbit/models/pod.glb (nose +Y in Blender, about 1 unit) and every ship uses it, tinted by the Paint material. Next: real-phone feel test, sound, own-ship prediction when on a TV.

games.name: Lost Sock
games.notes: v0.3: phone-as-screen. After scanning: 'Play on the TV (phone as controller)' or 'Play on your phone'. Phone screens get the map with the auto camera, pinch/pan anytime (eases back slowly), bottom bar with move, aim, jump, weapon menu and hold-to-charge FIRE; corner toggle flips between controller and phone screen. Mixed play shares one game; if everyone picks phones the first phone hosts and the TV is freed. Dev door entry (screen opened with ?dev=1) for the busy-screen queue. Next: real-phone test, phone-host 'move to TV', sound.

games.name: Demolition Derby
games.notes: v0.3.2: stick-aim steering is the default on controllers. The car turns to face where the stick points on screen; RT gas, LT brakes then reverses (aim behind to back up that way). A soft player-colour ring under the car, with a floating arrow while the stick is held. "Classic steering (left/right)" is in the gear panel. The phone joystick already steers this way. v0.3.1: up to 4 Xbox controllers join alongside phones (A joins / starts / boosts, left stick steers, RT gas, LT brake and reverse, RB boost, D-pad picks car and boost, X armour). A small gear opens controller settings (swap sticks). v0.3: Justin's sedan (sedan_v02.glb) for every car, tinted per player, with armour still attached. Damage goes to whichever parts face the hit (front, sides, rear, corners, crush from above): glass shatters; the hood dents, flaps while driving, then flies off; doors and trunk swing on their hinges, then break off; a wheel can come off (up to 2 per car; the car drives slower and pulls toward the missing wheel). Smoke past half damage, fire under the hood near the end. Loose parts become debris you can knock around, then fade after about 14 s. Camera about 12% closer. The AI plans for the coming edge. Armour now plays differently: None = fast with quicker boost refill, Plates = tanky and hard to shove but slower, Spikes = big contact damage and grinding. Boosts: Ram = unstoppable double-weight charge, Long = steerable steady push, Hop dash = jumps (can crush). Smarter AI: flanks to hit sides, picks weak cars, pushes toward drop-offs, reverses out when stuck, brakes at edges. Next: real-phone test; None armour still wins least in bot matches.

games.name: Red Deer Rescue
games.notes: Blockout: downtown to Bower Ponds, heroes auto-roam, mutant bunnies, phone votes. Dev launcher only.

games.name: Bloat Flier

games.name: Iron Stride Squad
games.notes: Dev build of asymmetric mechs, live Iron Stride untouched. Controller players get small fast Striders (twin-stick, MG, dash). Phone players get Titans: 6x bigger, slow, siege cannon, 8-missile barrage, stomp, with tap-to-walk and tap-to-lock map controls. Co-op vs drones and tanks. Every shot is tested against buildings. Next: real controller and phone test, a third-person TV camera, PvP.

games.name: Iron Stride open world
games.notes: Keyboard/mouse & controller = small fast Striders with centre reticle and canopy look (body follows, faster near edge; swap/invert respected). Phone = giant slow Titan with auto-calibrating aim. Big 1 km map of hills, mountains, ruined cities, bases, outposts; terrain and buildings block shots. Live v0.4.2 untouched.

games.name: Hop Top
games.notes: v0.1: 15-hole triangle peg solitaire. Pull any peg to start, jump to remove, rated at the end (Peg Legend = one peg left in the top hole). Undo + hint. Opening it on a phone plays solo; on a TV, phones share one board (co-op taps).

games.name: Dangerous Waters
games.notes: v0.1.1: renamed from Broadside to Dangerous Waters; space slot is now 'Dangerous Space Waters (coming)'. v0.1: Classic battleships, 10x10, five ships, using the cafe Battleship rules (cafe/js/games.js). TV shows both waters (hits/misses only); each phone holds its private fleet (shuffle, Ready) and fires on its turn. One phone = vs computer; phone pad also has 'play the computer on this phone'. Mode picker: Classic, Dangerous Space Waters (coming, disabled). Live cafe Battleship untouched.

games.name: Swish Flick
games.notes: v0.1.1: tall up-and-over arcs; flick speed sets arc height, flick length (short snap vs long sweep) sets distance; camera shows the apex. v0.1: Arcade hoop. Flick up on the phone to shoot (harder = farther, sideways = aim), backspin softens rim bounces, net swish. 45 s rounds: 2 pts, swish 3, 3-in-a-row bonus. Everyone shoots at once on the TV; works solo on one phone. Needs real-phone flick tuning.

games.name: Splash Clown
games.notes: v0.1.1: target has no stick, sits lower and slowly loops (along the bottom, up, across the top, down); throw as fast as you flick, several balls in flight at once (still 6 each). v0.1: Dunk tank. Flick a ball at the red target; a hit drops the proxy clown into the water (splash, sulks, climbs back, taunts on misses). 6 balls each, most dunks wins. TV with phones or solo on one phone.

games.name: Glide Puck
games.notes: v0.1: Air hockey, puck capped at about half real speed, drag your paddle with a finger, first to 7. Phone cams (corner button): Auto zoom, Radar (your half + a ping that grows as the puck comes), Follow (zoomed, soft-scroll, spring back so your half is in view before the puck is 20% in). Modes: vs computer on one phone, 2 phones (one hosts), or TV + 1-2 phones (computer fills a seat).

games.name: Stack Attack
games.notes: v0.1: Blocks appear on shelves; drag them onto the stand in 40 s, rotate with the button or a second-finger tap. Then a disaster: Earthquake, Tornado, or Big Lizard. Score = height still standing after it settles. Solo on a phone, or co-op on a TV with phones (matter.js physics).

games.name: Balloon Buddy
games.notes: v0.1.1: guess the word and Buddy lets go, lands on the grass and does a victory dance scaled by balloons left (7 = full bouncy jig, down to a wobbly one-balloon shuffle, labelled on screen), balloons float off, confetti stays. v0.1: Silly hangman. One player hides a word on their phone; the others tap letters. Each wrong letter pops one of Buddy's 7 balloons and he sinks toward a kiddie pool; out of balloons = a happy, soggy splash (floaties). Solo: Buddy picks the word. Phone-only: the host phone shows the scene and friends scan its code.
